title: AutoBE: restore a usable LLM budget for driver runs
description: Every configured provider path is dead as of 2026-09-10: (1) Zen free slugs (*-free) return MissingSessionID - free tier only works inside the OpenCode client; (2) Zen paid slugs (e.g. grok-4.6, deepseek-v4-flash) return CreditsError: insufficient balance; (3) zen/go/v1 also needs x-opencode-session, so the AutoBE driver cannot use it; (4) the local 127.0.0.1:8787 grok proxy used on 2026-09-02 is not running; (5) xAI direct returned 403 out-of-credits on the last attempt. Decision needed: top up the OpenCode Zen workspace, or point OPENCODE_BASE_URL/OPENCODE_API_KEY at another OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Verify a slug with a 1-token probe BEFORE launching a multi-hour phase run.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-11 00:45: workaround found — the OpenCode Go route works for the driver. Both Zen and Go require the x-opencode-session header (any UUID) + an OpenCode-ish User-Agent; the driver was missing that header, which is why every run 401'd with MissingSessionID. Go models (glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash, minimax-m3, kimi-k2.7-code) all tool-call and accept ~240k-token prompts. Free-tier slugs answer but die with FreeUsageLimitError mid-phase. Driver now also retries patiently (--attempts/--retryDelay) instead of 3 instant retries. Run in flight: systemd user unit autobe-go-run2, model glm-5.3, phases test->realize, log .autobe-state/generate-go.log. Remaining risk: the Go 5-hour/weekly cap is shared with OpenClaw and Hermes itself.
close_reason: Go route + session header works; AutoBE LLM loop abandoned in favor of hand-realize.
